investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. No preemption victims were found on those nodes, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window remained in a Pending/Unschedulable state for the full timeout duration (~121–147 s), preventing the agent from reaching a running/idle/ready state and causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to go uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules
possibleCauses: Primary: The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have their extended resource quota fully consumed by existing peer-pod workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new eval pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes.

Secondary: A prior eval run or production workload created remote agent pods that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to release resources, but if a prior run leaked pods, capacity would remain exhausted.

Tertiary: The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, so even if other nodes had spare general capacity, they cannot be used. A misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could artificially narrow the eligible node pool.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node removal, node NotReady) may have reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent eval probes, but no node-health signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create were observed with the same cluster state, it would suggest the failure is intermittent or race-conditioned rather than a hard capacity ceiling.

If the 4 non-affinity nodes were shown to be eligible for remote agent pods under a different affinity configuration and the pods scheduled successfully there, the root cause would be the overly restrictive affinity rule rather than absolute capacity exhaustion.
If evidence showed that the withCleanup wrapper successfully released all prior eval pods before this run, leaked pod accumulation would be ruled out as a contributing factor.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T18:42–18:47Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the only 2 eligible nodes in the 6-node production cluster, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers a kata peer-pod VM allocation that the scheduler cannot satisfy. Because agent creation never completes, the state-polling step that follows it also never executes, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and causing the contract validation to fail entirely.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract at line 264 requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none of which can be populated without a running pod.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion: both kata-capable nodes in the 6-node cluster are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for a new peer-pod VM. This is directly stated in all three scheduler messages (evidence ids: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, so even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were freed, the 4 remaining nodes would still be ineligible.

TERTIARY — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: another workload or a prior eval run may have allocated the available VM slots and not yet released them, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioned for peak eval load: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote-agent pods than is currently demanded, making exhaustion a recurring risk rather than a one-time event.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to run peer-pod workloads. No preemption victims were found on those nodes, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window remained in a Pending/Unschedulable state for the full timeout duration (~121–147 s), preventing the agent from reaching a running/idle/ready state and causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to go uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler reason, pod stuck for 144s, latencyMs=147521

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied if the pod never schedules
possibleCauses: Primary: The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have their extended resource quota fully consumed by existing peer-pod workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new eval pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes.

Secondary: A prior eval run or production workload created remote agent pods that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to release resources, but if a prior run leaked pods, capacity would remain exhausted.

Tertiary: The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, so even if other nodes had spare general capacity, they cannot be used. A misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could artificially narrow the eligible node pool.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node removal, node NotReady) may have reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent eval probes, but no node-health signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.

Tertiary — a concurrent load spike or leaked/stuck agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new scheduling. This is plausible but not directly evidenced in the packet.

Lower probability — a misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more slots than any single node provides) that makes scheduling structurally impossible. Would require inspecting the pod spec to confirm or rule out.

reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable scheduler message if the capacity issue persists.

reproductionSteps.details: All three should fail with the kata.peerpods.io/vm Unschedulable message if the root cause is cluster-wide capacity exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and compare Allocatable vs. Requests to confirm exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots
reproductionSteps.details: Query the cluster for pods with a kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request to identify whether leaked or stuck agent pods are holding capacity.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm as the exhausted resource on the 2 eligible nodes, blocking all remote agent pod creation.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata-capable nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner branch at line 1913-1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; pod scheduling failure prevents any evidence from being collected, causing a full contract gap.

affectedAreas.reason: Required sibling check (required=true, line 183) also failed with the same Unschedulable message, indicating the scheduling failure affects the entire remote-agents feature lifecycle.

affectedAreas.label: AURA eval check: remote-agent-state (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: Required sibling check (required=true, line 184) also failed with the same Unschedulable message, confirming no remote agent pod reached the state-polling stage.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether slots are fully consumed and by which pods.
Identify and terminate any leaked, stuck, or zombie remote-agent pods that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads, to restore scheduling capacity.

If capacity is structurally insufficient for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads, consider increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable limit on existing nodes or adding additional kata-capable nodes to the pool.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to determine whether the 4 non-kata nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by installing the kata peer-pod runtime on additional nodes), reducing single-pool pressure.
Add a cluster-level alert for kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization approaching 100% on the eligible node pool so capacity exhaustion is detected before it causes eval or production scheduling failures.

Note that this is an eval-layer failure detected by the AURA observability system. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; do not treat this as a confirmed production user-facing outage until cluster state is inspected.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested on the 2 eligible nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the capacity exhaustion hypothesis by showing how many VM slots are allocatable and how many are currently requested.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Replace <kata-node-selector> with the actual label used by the remote-agent pod's node affinity.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, ns: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked, stuck, or long-running agent pods are consuming all available VM slots and preventing new scheduling.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Look for pods in non-Running or non-Completed phases that may be holding slots without doing useful work.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe to check if the condition is still active
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is ongoing or was transient at the time of the original run.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: A pass on re-run would suggest a transient spike; a continued fail confirms sustained capacity exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect the pending remote-agent pod spec for node affinity and resource requests
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Reveals the exact node affinity rules and kata.peerpods.io/vm request quantity, confirming whether the 4-node affinity mismatch and the 2-node exhaustion are both structural.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: The pod name can be found from the scheduler event logs or by listing pods in a Pending state.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are not fully consumed, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a misconfiguration in the pod resource request would become the primary suspect.
If a subsequent eval run succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent agent creation) rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.
If the remote-agent pod spec requests a kata.peerpods.io/vm quantity greater than the per-node allocatable maximum, the root cause would be a pod spec misconfiguration rather than runtime exhaustion.
If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with scheduling errors, the problem may be broader than the kata peer-pod node pool.
If the 4 non-kata nodes show a different Unschedulable reason unrelated to node affinity (e.g., resource pressure), the affinity/selector diagnosis for those nodes would need revision.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the eligible node pool and fails with a warning before full exhaustion (e.g., at 80% utilization).

Add a pre-flight scheduling check eval that submits a dry-run pod (using kubectl --dry-run=server) for the remote-agent pod spec and asserts it is schedulable, catching capacity or affinity misconfigurations before a full agent lifecycle probe is attempted.

Add an eval that counts currently-pending or stuck remote-agent pods and fails if any pod has been in Pending/Unschedulable state for longer than a configurable threshold, catching leaked pods before they exhaust capacity.
Consider a sibling eval that verifies local-agent checks pass when remote-agent checks fail, to confirm the failure is isolated to the kata peer-pod node pool and not a broader cluster or API issue.
